title: Valid or not? scenarios
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: valid or not? scenarios)
intro: Lesson 12: Salah: its conditions (shurut). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Conditions come first
points: A condition is in place before salah begins
It continues through the whole salah
Miss one: the salah is not valid

head: Condition
In short
rows: Intending the prayer in the heart

panels.title: Time and qiblah
points: Prayer is prescribed at set times (4:103)
Turn your face towards al-Masjid al-Haram (2:144)
In the UK the qiblah is roughly south-east

questions.q: Hamza prays 'Asr before its time has begun.
questions.a: Condition: the time. Not valid; pray again once the time begins.

questions.q: Layla prays on a mat with a dry urine stain on it.
questions.a: Condition: removing najasah from the place. Not valid; pray on a clean place.

questions.q: Ali tries his best to find the qiblah, but faces the wrong way.
questions.a: Condition: the qiblah. Valid: he tried his best.

questions.q: Musa prays Dhuhr, then remembers he had not made wudu since using the toilet.
questions.a: Condition: purity from hadath. Not valid; make wudu and pray again.

questions.q: Sara prays with clothes that do not cover her 'awrah.
questions.a: Condition: covering the 'awrah. Not valid; cover properly and pray again.

keywords.def: conditions: things needed before and during salah
the parts of the body that must be covered

questions.q: Explain why covering the 'awrah is a condition of salah.
questions.a: Allah commands modest dress for prayer; without it the prayer is not valid.

questions.q: Facing the Ka'bah is called facing the ...
Which ayah says prayer has set times?

Five 'valid or not?' scenarios on the pupil PDF: write the condition involved and the ruling (e.g. praying Asr before its time; praying on a mat with a dry urine stain; praying facing the wrong way after trying your best to find the qiblah).
questions.a: Rulings with the condition named; the person who tried hard and erred in qiblah: prayer valid

questions.q: Extend: what if someone cannot work out the qiblah?
questions.a: Try their best; the prayer is valid even if they were wrong.

questions.q: Stretch: why is the niyyah a condition rather than something said aloud?
questions.a: Intention is in the heart; the Prophet ﷺ did not say a set phrase aloud.

questions.q: Which is a condition, not a pillar?
questions.a: A) Facing the qiblah. Facing the qiblah is needed before and during; al-Fatihah and ruku' are pillars inside the prayer.

questions.q: Praying before the time begins is ...
Think again: does Dhuhr before its time count?
questions.a: No: the time is a condition; pray it again in its time.
